headline: THE LAST PAYMENT IS DECIDED BEFORE THE FIRST POST HOLE
hook: The last post is plumb, the gate swings clean, and the homeowner who used to text you every morning has gone quiet. That balance was decided before the first post hole, at his kitchen table, when he signed a page with a total at the bottom and not one line tying the money to finished work.
angle: A crew's pull on the money shrinks with every finished phase, so the last payment is decided at signing: each payment tied in writing to a named, finished phase, and nothing extra built without a signed change order. A bigger deposit isn't the fix. The schedule is.

verdicts.headline: THE JOB WAS LOST AT THE KITCHEN TABLE
verdicts.verdict: Right moment, right turn, but "the job was lost" reads like a lost bid, not a stalled payment, so the headline blurs the angle. Its kitchen-table image now carries the winner's hook.

verdicts.headline: THE LAST POST IS SET AND HE STOPPED ANSWERING
verdicts.verdict: The hardest gut stop on the list, in the reader's own words, but it is all pain and no take: nothing says the fix lives at signing. Its opening moment now leads the winner's hook.

verdicts.headline: 17 MILLION VIEWS ON A TEARDOWN NOBODY SHOULD NEED
verdicts.verdict: Its number is a viral view count from secondary press, not a source OPS should rest a title on, it dates the post to one September 2026 video, and it leads with the crowbar instead of the fix.

verdicts.headline: THE $1,000 RULE EVERY CREW SHOULD STEAL
verdicts.verdict: A real primary-source number, but it is one state's rule about having a written contract, not about when the money moves, so most readers get a rule that isn't theirs and the schedule goes unnamed.

verdicts.headline: THE FINAL PAYMENT IS DECIDED BEFORE THE FIRST HOLE
verdicts.verdict: Winner: the only headline that states the whole angle in a foreman's words, on a real job-site moment, with no claim the sources can't back and nothing that dates. Sharpened to "last payment" and "first post hole".

verdicts.headline: A BIGGER DEPOSIT WON'T GET YOU PAID
verdicts.verdict: The best belief-turn in the room and grounded in California's deposit cap, but it attacks the wrong fix without naming the right one, and "won't get you paid" overstates it. Its tension moved into the winner's angle.

verdicts.headline: WOULD YOU TEAR OUT A FENCE TO GET PAID?
verdicts.verdict: Stops the thumb, but it reopens the justice-versus-lawsuit fight the post means to leave, edges toward endorsing self-help removal, and ties the title to one viral video.

verdicts.headline: WHAT DOES YOUR CONTRACT SAY ABOUT THE LAST PAYMENT?
verdicts.verdict: Specific and useful, it sends the owner straight to the paperwork, but it reads like a lawyer's newsletter and lacks the gut stop a busy owner needs between jobs.

verdicts.headline: YOU'RE EITHER PAID BY THE PHASE OR CHASING THE BALANCE
verdicts.verdict: Carries the angle, but "paid by the phase" is office talk, and the either-or shape echoes "COUNT THE HOURS OR COUNT THE LOSSES" from 2026-09-15.

verdicts.headline: YOU'RE EITHER WRITING CHANGE ORDERS OR GIVING WORK AWAY
verdicts.verdict: The wider-gate moment is sharp, but change orders are half the move, so this sells a narrower post, and the either-or shape repeats the 2026-09-15 title.

verdicts.headline: FINISHED WORK DESERVES A FINISHED PAYMENT
verdicts.verdict: A bumper sticker: wordplay with no moment, number or mechanism, and nothing a skeptical owner would stop to argue with.

verdicts.headline: NO CREW SHOULD HAVE TO BEG FOR EARNED MONEY
verdicts.verdict: Heart without a take. Every owner agrees and nobody learns where the fix lives, so it fails specific over clever and carries no angle.
